conversation.user: I'm studying Construction Management Bachelor of Technology.
conversation.advisor:
You’re studying the **Bachelor of Technology in Construction Management**, an active degree-completion program at BCIT’s **School of Construction and the Environment**.

- **Location:** Burnaby  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **Study options:** Full-time or part-time  
- **Program focus:** Construction-project management, technical skills, and interpersonal leadership

The curriculum includes:

- **Construction Controls and Techniques:** CMGT 7160, CMGT 7190, CMGT 7211, CMGT 7400  
- **Organization Management:** BUSA 7250, CMGT 7330, CMGT 7420, CMGT 8435  
- **Stakeholder Engagement:** CMGT 7535, CMGT 7660, CMGT 8602  
- **Management electives:** At least **4 credits from the approved management-elective pool**  
- **Liberal Studies:** At least **12 credits**; part-time students may replace LIBS 7013 with 3 additional approved Liberal Studies elective credits  
- **Professional Standards:** CMGT 7810, CMGT 8211, CMGT 8700, plus a choice of **one** final project: CMGT 8800 or CMGT 8810

The program’s stored source is available here:  
https://www.bcit.ca/programs/construction-management-bachelor-of-technology-full-time-part-time-8800btech/

courses.course_overview: The goal of this course is to provide the student with an opportunity to work independently on an applied research project associated with a construction industry issue or procedure. Students work closely with an industry sponsor, under the mentorship of a faculty advisor to execute the research proposal that was developed in CMGT 8700. The students' pre-approved proposal outlines the project scope, goals, methods, and deliverables that forms the basis for this course. This course is intended to assess the students' ability to integrate the skills and knowledge gained from the Program with their individual work experience and apply these in a real-world context. In conjunction with an industry sponsor, the student solves a technical problem relating to construction. The research project must contain elements that are innovative, experimental, or exploratory in nature. A faculty advisor will supervise the progress of the project, provide guidance and direction where appropriate and evaluate the final report and its presentation. The faculty advisor submits their evaluation and the final grade is determined collaboratively with the Department.

No. You previously told me that you **have not completed CMGT 8800 — Industry Based Project**, so I can’t mark the final-project requirement complete.

The program requires completion of **CMGT 8700 — Industry Based Project Proposal**, followed by **one** of:

- **CMGT 8800 — Industry Based Project**
- **CMGT 8810 — Industry Based Project**

Program details: https://www.bcit.ca/programs/construction-management-bachelor-of-technology-full-time-part-time-8800btech/
